'''Robert Tijdeman''' (born 30 July 1943 in [[Oostzaan]], [[North Holland]]) is a Dutch mathematician. Specializing in [[number theory]], he is best known for his [[Tijdeman's theorem]]. He is a professor of mathematics at the [[Leiden University]] since 1975, and was chairman of the department of mathematics and computer science at Leiden from 1991 to 1993. He was also president of the [[Royal Dutch Mathematical Society]] from 1984 to 1986.<ref name="cv">[http://www.math.leidenuniv.nl/~tijdeman/cvnew.pdf Curriculum vitae] from Tijdeman's web site, retrieved 2009-08-26.</ref>

Tijdeman received his PhD in 1969 from the [[University of Amsterdam]],<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=45998}}</ref> and received an honorary doctorate from [[University of Debrecen|Kossuth Lajos University]] in 1999. In 1987 he was elected to the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{cite web |author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/nl/leden/leden/4869 |title=Rob Tijdeman |language=Dutch |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |access-date=15 July 2015 |archive-date=15 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150715083613/https://www.knaw.nl/nl/leden/leden/4869 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Research==

In [[number theory]], '''[[Tijdeman's theorem]]'''<ref>{{citation |first=Robert |last=Tijdeman |title=On the equation of Catalan |journal=[[Acta Arithmetica]] |volume=29 |issue=2 |year=1976 |pages=197–209 |doi= 10.4064/aa-29-2-197-209| zbl=0286.10013 |doi-access=free }}</ref> states that there are at most a finite number of consecutive powers. Stated another way, the set of solutions in integers ''x'', ''y'', ''n'', ''m'' of the [[exponential diophantine equation]]

:<math>y^m = x^n + 1,</math>

for exponents ''n'' and ''m'' greater than one, is finite.<ref name="rnt20c">{{ citation | pages=352 | title=Rational Number Theory in the 20th Century: From PNT to FLT | series=Springer Monographs in Mathematics | first=Wladyslaw | last=Narkiewicz | publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] | year=2011 | isbn=978-0-857-29531-6 }}</ref><ref>{{citation | last=Schmidt | first=Wolfgang M. | authorlink=Wolfgang M. Schmidt | title=Diophantine approximations and Diophantine equations | series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics | volume=1467 | publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] | year=1996 | edition=2nd | isbn=978-3-540-54058-8 | zbl=0754.11020 | page=207 }}</ref> (This was a significant step towards resolving [[Catalan’s conjecture]], which [[Preda Mihăilescu]] accomplished in 2002.)

Tijdeman worked closely with [[Tarlok Nath Shorey|T.N. Shorey]] on various arithmetic problems. He has also worked on algorithms  in the area of [[discrete tomography]].
